reducing-air-pollutants-s2.title: A passage on a sulfur dioxide trading program
reducing-air-pollutants-s2.html:
A state council is debating a plan to cut sulfur dioxide from its twelve coal power plants. Under the plan, the state sets a total cap on SO2 for all plants together and lowers it by 5% each year. Each plant receives permits for its share. A plant that cuts its emissions below its permits, for example by installing a scrubber or switching to low-sulfur coal, may sell the extra permits to a plant that finds cutting more expensive. Supporters say the cap guarantees the total cut while letting the cheapest cuts happen first. Critics worry that a plant buying many permits could keep polluting its own neighborhood, and they ask the council to add a limit for each plant as well as the total cap.

Invented passage for practice.

items.q: Write a policy that would cut sulfur dioxide from a state's coal power plants, and say how it works.

specific.frame: The state passes ___, so plants ___, which reduces the SO2 in the air.

action.label: Policy
options: a law capping the SO2 each coal plant may release each year
better smokestacks for every coal plant
a campaign asking residents to save electricity

why.1: Smokestacks are a technology, not a law or rule; the question asks for a policy.
why.2: A voluntary campaign is not a rule, and it does not target SO2 directly.

how.label: How it works
options: raise their smokestacks to spread the SO2 farther
burn low-sulfur coal or remove SO2 from their exhaust to stay under the cap
release more NOx in place of SO2

why.0: Taller stacks move SO2 farther away; they do not lower the amount released.
why.2: Trading one pollutant for another does not lower air pollution.

specific.model: The state passes a law capping the SO2 each coal plant may release each year, so plants burn low-sulfur coal or remove SO2 from their exhaust to stay under the cap, which reduces the SO2 in the air.

items.q: Propose a city-level solution, other than a rule on paints, that would reduce photochemical smog, and say how it works.

specific.frame: The city could ___, which reduces ___, so less ozone forms in sunlight.

action.label: Solution
options: expand bus and light-rail service so fewer people drive to work
limit the solvents allowed in house paints
plant more trees that release VOCs

why.1: The question says other than a rule on paints.
why.2: Trees that release VOCs would add an ingredient of smog, not remove one.

what.label: What it reduces
options: the CO2 that traps heat
the NOx and VOCs from car exhaust
the sulfur dioxide from coal plants

why.0: CO2 is not an ingredient of photochemical smog.
why.2: SO2 is not the driver of photochemical smog; NOx and VOCs are.

specific.model: The city could expand bus and light-rail service so fewer people drive, which reduces the NOx and VOCs from car exhaust, so less ozone forms in sunlight.

items.q: A valley town has frequent winter inversions. Propose a town rule that would reduce the pollution that builds up during them, and explain how it works.

specific.frame: The town could ___, which reduces ___ while the inversion traps the air.

rule.label: Rule
options: ban wood stove and fireplace burning on days an inversion is forecast
require taller chimneys on every house
move the weather station out of the valley

why.1: Smoke from a taller chimney still stops under the warm layer, and it does not cut emissions.
why.2: Moving the station changes the measurement, not the pollution.

what.label: What it reduces
options: the heat that forms the warm layer
the smoke and fine particles released into the trapped air
the sunlight that reaches the valley

why.0: Wood stoves do not cause the warm layer; it forms from the weather.
why.2: Sunlight helps break the inversion; cutting it would make things worse.

specific.model: The town could ban wood stove burning on days an inversion is forecast, which reduces the smoke and fine particles released into the trapped air, so their concentration does not build up.

Air normally cools with height, so the temperature at 1,000 m is lower: 4 - 6.5 = -2.5 °C.

items.q: Desert dust from a dried-up lake bed blows into a nearby town. Propose a solution that reduces this dust, and explain how it works.

specific.frame: Managers could ___, which reduces dust because ___.

action.label: Solution
options: return some water to the lake bed and plant native shrubs on the exposed areas
require cleaner engines on cars in the town
build a taller smokestack at the nearest power plant

why.1: Cleaner engines cut car exhaust gases, not dust from a lake bed.
why.2: A smokestack has nothing to do with lake bed dust.

how.label: How it works
options: wet or covered soil cannot be lifted by the wind
plants release more CO2 into the air

why.1: Plants take in CO2 by photosynthesis; this is not how the solution works.
why.2: An inversion would trap dust, not reduce it.

specific.model: Managers could return some water to the lake bed and plant native shrubs on the exposed areas, which reduces dust because wet or covered soil cannot be lifted by the wind.

options: A radon test kit placed in the basement

items.q: A family uses a wood stove that releases 25 grams of PM2.5 per hour of burning. They burn it 6 hours a day for 120 days each winter. Write the setup, with units, for the PM2.5 released in one winter, in kilograms, then the answer.

mistakes.why: That is the answer in grams. Multiply by 1 kg / 1,000 g to convert to kilograms.
The conversion factor is upside down. Grams must be on the bottom so they cancel.
18,000 is in grams. Divide by 1,000 for kilograms: 18 kg.

items.q: In a rural village, families cook over open wood fires inside their homes. Propose a solution that reduces indoor air pollution and explain how it works.

specific.frame: The village could ___, which reduces indoor smoke because ___.

action.label: Solution
options: provide efficient cookstoves with chimneys that vent outdoors
install radon fans under every home
ban cooking indoors during summer

why.1: Radon fans remove soil gas, not smoke from cooking fires.
why.2: A seasonal ban is not realistic for daily cooking and does not fix the stove.

how.label: How it works
options: the stove burns wood more completely and the chimney carries smoke outside
the chimney filters out the CO2 so it cannot warm the house
the stove turns smoke particles into ozone

why.1: The health problem is smoke particles and CO, not CO2 warming the house.
why.2: Stoves do not turn particles into ozone, which would also be harmful.

specific.model: The village could provide efficient cookstoves with chimneys that vent outdoors, which reduces indoor smoke because the stove burns wood more completely and the chimney carries the smoke outside.

items.q: What percent of the plant's sulfur dioxide does the wet scrubber remove?

mistakes.why: 5% is the share that is left (2,000 of 40,000). The scrubber removes the other 95%.
That is the fraction. Multiply by 100 for a percent: 95%.

items.q: Which pollutant's emissions were cut by the largest percent?
options: Sulfur dioxide, cut by the wet scrubber
Particulate matter
Nitrogen oxides, by a lower burner temperature
Carbon dioxide, by the new controls

items.q: Why did the new controls not lower the plant's CO2?
options: The devices remove SO2 and particles, not CO2
The scrubber turns the SO2 into extra CO2
CO2 is a particle that the precipitator missed
Less CO2 forms when coal burns at a lower temperature

items.q: Lowering the burner temperature cut NOx by 20%. Why does burning at a lower temperature reduce NOx?
options: A cooler flame burns off the nitrogen in the coal first
Lower heat turns NOx into sulfur dioxide
A cooler flame makes the scrubber work on NOx too
Less air nitrogen joins oxygen in a cooler flame

items.q: What is the main claim made by the plan's supporters?
options: Each plant should be required to install the same scrubber
SO2 should be cut mainly to slow global climate warming
A cap with trading cuts SO2 at low cost
Plants that buy permits will clean up their neighborhoods

items.q: What assumption underlies the critics' concern?
options: A cap will fail to lower the total SO2 from the twelve plants
SO2 harms people most near the plant that releases it
Scrubbers do not remove SO2 from a plant's exhaust
Low-sulfur coal costs more than ordinary coal everywhere

items.q: Which evidence would best support the supporters' claim?
options: A past cap-and-trade plan met its goal for less money

Coal plants also release mercury and CO2

items.q: Is the plan described in the passage a policy or a technology?
options: A technology, because scrubbers are one way to meet it
A technology, because it uses permits that can be sold
Neither, because it does not name a pollutant to cut
A policy, because it is a rule plants follow

items.q: Which device in a car changes carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and unburned hydrocarbons into less harmful gases?
options: A wet scrubber
An electrostatic precipitator

items.q: How does an electrostatic precipitator remove particles from a smokestack?
options: It sprays a limestone slurry that reacts with the particles
It charges particles and collects them on plates

items.q: A wet scrubber sprays a mixture of water and crushed limestone into a coal plant's exhaust. What does it remove, and how?
options: SO2, which reacts with limestone and is caught

items.q: A city wants to cut its NOx and VOCs from traffic without new technology on cars. Which approach fits best?

items.q: A cement plant releases 5,000 metric tons of particulates a year. A baghouse filter captures 99.5% of them. Write the setup for the particulates still released each year, then the answer.

mistakes.why: That is the amount captured. The question asks what is still released: 100% - 99.5% = 0.5%.
Divide the percent by 100 to turn it into a fraction.
4,975 metric tons is what the baghouse captures. Subtract it from 5,000 to get what is released.

items.q: Explain how a catalytic converter reduces smog, naming the pollutant it changes and what it becomes.

specific.frame: A catalytic converter changes ___ into ___, which reduces smog because ___.

input.label: Pollutant changed
options: nitrogen oxides
sulfur dioxide
carbon dioxide

why.1: SO2 is removed from smokestacks by scrubbers, not by car converters.
why.2: The converter makes CO2; it does not remove it.

output.label: What it becomes
options: ozone
nitrogen gas and oxygen
nitric acid

why.0: Making ozone would add smog, not reduce it.
why.2: Nitric acid is a secondary pollutant; the converter makes harmless N2.

because.label: Why that reduces smog
options: less NOx is left to react with VOCs in sunlight to form ozone
nitrogen gas absorbs sunlight before it reaches the ground
the converter cools the air above the city

why.1: N2 does not block sunlight; the benefit is fewer ozone-making ingredients.
why.2: The converter does not change the air temperature.

specific.model: A catalytic converter changes nitrogen oxides into nitrogen gas and oxygen, which reduces smog because less NOx is left to react with VOCs in sunlight to form ozone.

items.q: Describe the relationship between SO2 emissions and rain pH shown in the graph.

items.q: Which explanation connects the two lines?
options: SO2 forms sulfuric acid, so less SO2 means less acid
SO2 is a base that raises the pH of rain

items.q: Find the percent change in the region's SO2 emissions from 1980 to 2020.

mistakes.why: You divided by the 2020 value. Divide by the old (1980) value, 24 million metric tons.
Emissions fell, so the change is negative: -87.5%.

items.q: Each drop of 1 in pH means 10 times more acidic. How many times more acidic was the rain in 1980 (pH 4.2) than in 2020 (pH 5.2)?

mistakes.why: 1 is the difference in pH. Each step of 1 is a factor of 10, so the answer is 10 times.
pH is a logarithmic scale; do not divide the pH values. A difference of 1 means 10 times.

items.q: All four lakes get the same acid rain. Why are Mill Lake and Clay Lake near neutral pH?

items.q: Using the rule that each drop of 1 in pH means 10 times more acidic, how many times more acidic is North Lake (pH 4.8) than Clay Lake (pH 7.4)? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

mistakes.why: 2.6 is the pH difference. Each unit is a factor of 10: use 10 to the power 2.6.
You multiplied 2.6 by 10. The scale is logarithmic: 10 to the power 2.6.

items.q: A town wants to restore fish to North Lake quickly while emissions keep falling. Which step works fastest, and what is its drawback?

items.q: A coal plant builds a very tall smokestack so its town's air meets SO2 limits. What is an unintended effect?

items.q: A lake's pH fell from 6.5 to 4.5 after years of acid rain. Write the setup for how many times more acidic it became, then the answer.

mistakes.why: That is the drop in pH. Each unit of pH is a factor of 10, so raise 10 to that power.
pH is logarithmic: a drop of 2 means 10 × 10, not 2 × 10.
A drop of 2 in pH is 10 × 10 = 100 times, not 2 × 10.
2 is the change in pH. The acidity changed by 10 to the power 2: 100 times.

items.q: Propose a policy that would reduce acid deposition across a whole country, and explain how it works.

specific.frame: The country could pass ___, which reduces acid deposition by ___.

policy.label: Policy
options: a law capping SO2 and NOx from power plants and vehicles
a program to add limestone to every acidic lake
a rule requiring taller smokestacks at power plants

why.1: Liming treats lakes one at a time; it does not reduce acid deposition.
why.2: Taller stacks spread SO2 farther; they do not cut it.

how.label: How it works
options: cutting the gases that form sulfuric and nitric acid in the air
neutralizing the acid after it falls
blowing the acid out to sea

why.1: That describes liming, a treatment after the fact, not a cut in deposition.
why.2: Moving the acid elsewhere is not a reduction.

specific.model: The country could pass a law capping SO2 and NOx from power plants and vehicles, which reduces acid deposition by cutting the gases that form sulfuric and nitric acid in the air, so less acid falls in rain.

items.q: Sounds at or above 85 dB can damage hearing over time. Which measured sounds are at or above that level?

Lunch, recess and the road work

items.q: The decibel scale is logarithmic: each 10 dB step means 10 times the sound intensity. How does the 100 dB road work compare with the 80 dB playground at recess?
options: It has 100 times the sound intensity

It has 2 times the sound intensity

items.q: Using the rule that each 10 dB means 10 times the intensity, how many times more intense is the 110 dB jet noise than the 80 dB playground at recess?

mistakes.why: 30 is the difference in dB. Each 10 dB is a factor of 10, so 30 dB is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000.
You multiplied the 30 dB difference by 10. The scale is logarithmic: three steps of 10 is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000.

items.q: A machine is 95 dB at the operator's ear. Wearing earmuffs lowers it to 75 dB. Using the rule that each 10 dB is 10 times the intensity, write the setup for how many times less intense the sound is with earmuffs, then the answer.

mistakes.why: That is the drop in dB. Each 10 dB is a factor of 10: raise 10 to (95 - 75) / 10.

items.q: Shipping lanes run through waters where whales feed. Propose a solution that reduces the harm from ship noise, and explain how it works.

specific.frame: Managers could ___, which reduces harm because ___.

action.label: Solution
options: set slower speed limits for ships in whale feeding areas
ban whales from the shipping lanes
require ships to carry earmuffs for the crew

why.1: Whales cannot be banned from where their food is.
why.2: Earmuffs protect the crew, not the whales.

how.label: How it works
options: slower propellers make less underwater noise, so whale calls are masked less
slower ships release more oxygen into the water
slower ships make the water warmer for whales

why.1: Ship speed does not add oxygen to the water.
why.2: Ship speed does not warm the water in a way that helps whales.

specific.model: Managers could set slower speed limits for ships in whale feeding areas, which reduces harm because slower propellers make less underwater noise, so whale calls are masked less.
